title: She Spent Twenty Years Missing The Boy Who Ate Tofu . . . (Tune In for Love)
caption:
Tune In for Love (2019): a bakery girl and a boy fresh out of juvenile detention keep missing each other for twenty years.
A slow, gentle Korean love story about timing. Follow for more movie recaps!

#tuneinforlove #koreanmovie #movierecap #romance #spoilerroom
comment: Would you run across the city for someone like Mia did? Why?

segments.say: Twenty years of missing each other, and now Mia is *running*.
To see how it got here, go back to 1994, and a tiny *bakery*.
Mia works the counter at Misu Bakery with her best friend *Ruby*.
One morning a stiff boy in a school uniform walks in and asks for something made with *soybeans*.
Ruby takes one look at him. I bet he just got out of *jail*.
She is right. Henry spent his teens in a juvenile *detention* center.
In there, a late-night radio show was the only thing that kept him *sane*.
Out here, he spots a sign in the window. Part-timer *wanted*.
Mia gives him the job, and soon Henry is kneading *dough*.
He says he hates bread. But he keeps showing up, just to stand near *Mia*.
Then Christmas comes, and the little bakery glows with *lights*.
That's when Henry's old crew from the detention center walk in, loud, and drag him *out*.
They pull him into a bar, and one drink turns into a whole *night*.
The night ends badly, and Henry disappears. Soon a sign goes up on the door. *Closed*.
Three years later, Mia is a college student, desperate for a *job*.
A part-time spot at a radio station opens up. Only two months, but it's *hers*.
She celebrates with Ruby, who now runs a noodle *restaurant*.
Walking home that night, Mia runs into *Henry*.
He's heading into the army tomorrow. So they stay up all *night*.
She patches him up in her tiny room, and they talk like no time has *passed*.
She lends him Ruby's old clothes, and they fit him *perfectly*.
In the morning, he makes her promise to write. Check your inbox, he *says*.
Henry writes from the army, and Mia writes back every *night*.
But the replies slow down, and her inbox sits *unread*.
Silence hurts more than a goodbye.
Years later, the bakery where they met is torn *down*.
By the year 2000, Henry is back in the city, working at a gym and chatting with Mia online *again*.
She calls him from work just to hear his *voice*.
But then money goes missing at his job, and everyone blames *Henry*.
He starts a message to Mia, then deletes every word, and goes *silent*.
Mia tells herself she hates him. Then she cries on the *bus*.
Two people, one phone call apart.
Years go by. Mia becomes a writer at a radio *station*.
Then Henry sees an ad. A visual radio show needs a camera *operator*.
Somehow, they find each other again. For a while it is soft and *easy*.
They cook together, read in bed, and tease each other about the old *days*.
Mia still dreams of reopening the old bakery. She sketches the shop she *wants*.
But Henry won't talk about his past, and Mia can feel the *wall*.

segments.text: I wish you had told me.
I always prayed to God to let me live a normal life.

segments.say: Then his old crew pulls him back into a dark garage, and the fight gets *ugly*.
Henry sprints through the streets after Mia's *car*.
He catches her, and they hold each other in the middle of the *road*.
But she gets back in the car, and Henry is left alone on the *street*.
Mia ends up at Ruby's noodle shop, drinking alone, thinking about the tofu boy she can't *forget*.
She never stopped waiting for him.
At her desk, Mia listens to a radio show, and the host asks, whose name comes to *mind*?
She drops everything and *runs*, across the city, past the river, up the steps.
At the radio station, Henry is behind a camera when she steps into *view*.
She finds him, and for the first time in years, neither of them has to *run*.
Some love stories take a lifetime to line *up*.
